long_biography.plain_text:
Ventura de Paz studied medicine in Havana before leaving Cuba for the United States. In Miami he sold clothing at a flea market while looking for a foothold in healthcare. An ear, nose and throat specialist offered him work performing hearing tests, and he built up practical diagnostic experience. He and a physician partner started a diagnostic company with bank financing. When a run-down clinic in northwest Miami came up for sale, they bought it; de Paz continued alone after his partner withdrew.

Doctor's Medical Center grew from that beginning into a South Florida primary-care network with clinics serving Medicare, Medicaid and other patients. By the time Cano Health bought its operations in 2021, the group had 18 centres. The $300 million acquisition price was for the business and its multiple owners, not an audited sum received personally by de Paz. Although he was its founder and majority owner, the asset sale prevents treating the former clinics as his current operating company. His present principal holdings are not publicly established.
